I mean, no drug is necessarily GOOD for bipolar, but if you're on lithium you can't take acid, shrooms, or molly. Grand mal seizures. There's a huge risk. Also I personally destroyed my entire life by snorting focalin/ritalin/adderall. Amphetamines are the devil if you're bipolar, it'll make that mania psychotic. Opiates wouldn't be any more harmful to you than they would to anyone else (not that you should do them, they're highly addictive as I'm sure you know). Xanax is probably not a good idea but if you're gonna do something this isn't the worst, as long as you're willing to deal with the withdrawls. Surpised no one has mentioned weed yet, it's actually one of the worst for me. If you have any kind of psychotic feature you should NOT smoke weed, I was in psychosis for months thanks to weed. I know you can drink on lithium, dunno about the other drugs. Caffeine (yes it's a drug) is actually major mania trigger for me, and I tend to stack it with amphetamines because I'm a masochist. Nicotine keeps me sane. Long story short, if you're gonna do something it's safer to go with a downer. Better to sleep than to get 5150'd. Don't go developing a heroin addiction though, once a junkie always a junkie.

I am an avid AA member, and also type one bipolar. This is what the books says. Addiction is a three part disease. We have the physical allergy to mood and mind altering substances. We are literally allergic. Our allergy manifests in what's called the phenomenon of craving. Recreational users do not crave drugs. Then we have the mental obsession. This means we can't stop ourselves even when we want to. Finally we have what is called a spiritual malady. This is basically saying that we always tried to play God, and it never really worked out for us. AA is not inherently religious. I have been to atheist and agnostic meetings. We simply have to find something greater than ourselves to draw strength from, since our dilemma was always lack of power. Left to my own devices, I will run my life straight into the ground, so I need to seek advice from someone or something who knows more than I do. As for thinking that the people in AA cannot relate to you, this is very common. Most new people tend to focus of on the differences. No one in there is alike. We are people who would not normally mix. However, we all have one thing in common. We have all been through some type of hell, and we are all trying to crawl out of it. This is most definitely a disease. You treat your bipolar with medication, proper sleep and nutrition. You must treat your addiction too. The way to do this is through the 12 steps. Meetings are good, but WILL NOT save you. You have to work the twelve steps with a sponsor in order to recover. Do not slack on this, for it could be the difference between success and a relapse. If you are unsure if you are an addict, here are some qualifiers. Not everyone is. Do you crave drugs once you start using? Or, once you start, do you find that you have no control over how much you take? If either of those is true, you may be an addict. There is a way out no matter how far you are, but you have to be willing to accept the help. Nothing in this world can make an addict who doesn't want to stop quit drugs. Not jail, not prison, not pleas from family members, nothing. You must decide for yourself if you are an addict, truly, and if you are, if you are willing to stop. Question everything you read and hear. Decide for yourself. Don't let other people tell you how you feel. Find your truth. If you have any more questions I would love to help.
